features.label: Thirteen Colonies (Britain)
features.source: The mainland British colonies, represented using the later United States extent east of the imperial frontier used elsewhere in this dataset.

features.label: British North America
features.source: British North America after the Treaty of Paris; the later Canadian parts are used as a consistent modern-boundary approximation.

features.label: Florida (Britain)
features.source: Britain held East and West Florida between the Treaties of Paris.

features.label: British Guiana
features.source: The Essequibo, Demerara and Berbice colonies; Britain consolidated control during the Napoleonic era.

features.label: Newfoundland (Britain)
features.source: Britain's Newfoundland colony, represented with the later Labrador attachment for continuity.

features.label: British North America
features.source: The colonies and the Hudson's Bay Company's Rupert's Land. Stops short of the Oregon Country, which is drawn separately for as long as its ownership was open.

features.label: British North America
features.source: The Oregon Treaty gave Britain everything north of the 49th parallel, which is when that line first belongs on the map.

features.label: Rupert's Land (Britain)
features.source: What Confederation left out: Rupert's Land and the North-Western Territory, the Pacific colony, and the island.

features.label: British Arctic Territories
features.source: Held back at Confederation and transferred to Canada separately in 1880.

features.label: Newfoundland (Britain)
features.source: A colony, then a dominion in its own right, until it voted to join Canada.

features.label: Labrador (Britain)
features.source: Attached to Newfoundland in 1809 and drawn with it throughout. Kept as a span of its own so the mainland is named Labrador rather than taking the island's name, which is what a single span would do — the anchor goes to the larger piece.

features.label: Belize (Britain)
features.source: A logwood settlement held in fact under Spanish and then Guatemalan sovereignty, which is why it is drawn as contested until it became the colony of British Honduras.

features.label: Trinidad (Britain)
features.source: Taken by British expedition in 1797; shown as occupied until the Treaty of Amiens confirmed British possession.

features.label: St Lucia (Britain)
features.source: Changed hands between Britain and France repeatedly until Paris confirmed it as British in 1814; drawn as British throughout.

features.label: Falkland Islands (Britain)
features.source: Britain re-established administration in 1833 and has administered the islands since.
